translation_notes: translated.ldpy is byte-identical to original.py and transpiles unchanged: all 15 RDF operations of the module are opaque to the notation. 13 are SPARQL query strings passed to prepareQuery()/graph.query() (islands do not apply inside Python strings, by design), and the remaining two are Graph() + g.parse(path, format=f) in _guess_format_and_parse.

the prefix bindings the module does declare are dicts of strings passed as initNs= to prepareQuery ({'dcterms': 'http://purl.org/dc/terms/'}, {'rdf': rdflib.RDF}); ldpy's @prefix cannot feed them, so the same IRI is still written out by hand in each of the ten helpers -- exactly the duplication the notation is meant to remove, but out of its reach here
select_local_void_subject even builds a query by f-string interpolation of an IRI ('<{ds_uri}> dcterms:subject ?classUri'), where ldpy would want f<...>; inside a query string it cannot help

context shims (identical for both sides, imports unchanged): local config.py with the single Config.QUERY_LOV setting the region reads (kept at its upstream default True); src/util.py with CATEGORIES and match_file_lod copied verbatim (the rest of upstream util.py loads src/filter/filter.json at import time); src/lov_data_preparation.py stubbed to return [] because find_tags_from_list/find_comments_from_lists are HTTP clients for the LOV API -- the QUERY_LOV branch is still taken

driver fixture sample_dataset.ttl was written for this evaluation (not taken from the repository); it exercises all thirteen queries through process_file_full_inplace, which is the only module-level entry that reaches them
